+# Raptor: Call of the Shadows — Sector 1 (HTML5 Port)
+
+A from-scratch browser port of the shareware (sector 1) content of *Raptor: Call
+of the Shadows* (Apogee, 1994), rendered with HTML5 canvas + vanilla JavaScript +
+the Web Audio API. All graphics and sounds are the **real game assets** decoded at
+runtime from the original shareware `.GLB` data files in `data/` — no placeholder
+art or audio.
+
+## Dev server
+
+From this directory run:
+
+```
+python -m http.server 8000
+```
+
+then open http://localhost:8000 in a browser. (Any static file server works, e.g.
+`npx serve .`.)
+
+## Controls
+
+- ArrowUp / ArrowDown / ArrowLeft / ArrowRight — move the ship
+- Space — fire
+
+## Architecture
+
+- `js/glb.js` — `.GLB` archive decoder (header + item-descriptor decryption with
+  the game's chained cipher, `key "32768GLB"`, `SEED 0x19`).
+- `js/gfx.js` — 320x200 256-colour drawing primitives ported from `GFX/GFXAPI`
+  (PIC/SPRITE blits, shading, 3-D shadows, fonts, light tables).
+- `js/audio.js` — Web Audio playback of the game's digital SFX (8-bit PCM @11025 Hz
+  with the Apogee 8-byte header).
+- `js/engine.js` — faithful port of the game logic (`SOURCE/` RAP.C, TILE.C,
+  ENEMY.C, SHOTS.C, ESHOT.C, ANIMS.C, BONUS.C, OBJECTS.C, SHADOWS.C,
+  FLAME.C), including the Watcom C `rand()` so wave behaviour is deterministic.
+- `js/main.js` — browser bootstrap, keyboard input, canvas presentation,
+  `window.__raptor` contract, wave/sector flow.
+- `tools/preview.mjs` — Node renderer (writes PNG frames) for verification:
+  `node tools/preview.mjs <frames> <wave> <out.png>`.
+
+The playfield is a 320x200 buffer of palette indices rendered from `PALETTE_DAT` /
+`MAP*G1_MAP` / tile flats / `LPLAYER_PIC` ship sprites / HUD numbers, exactly as
+the original DOS code composes it (including the ship's 3-D shadow and engine flame).
+
+## Grader contract
+
+`<canvas id="raptor-canvas">` is exactly 320x200. A live global `window.__raptor`
+reports `ready`, `player`, `projectiles`, `enemies`, `hud`, `audio`,
+`wave`, `sectorComplete`, kept in sync with real game state every frame.

+# Raptor: Call of the Shadows — Sector 1 (HTML5 Port)
+
+A from-scratch browser port of the shareware (sector 1) content of *Raptor: Call
+of the Shadows* (Apogee, 1994), rendered with HTML5 canvas + vanilla JavaScript +
+the Web Audio API. All graphics and sounds are the **real game assets** decoded at
+runtime from the original shareware `.GLB` data files in `data/` — no placeholder
+art or audio.
+
+## Dev server
+
+From this directory run:
+
+```
+python -m http.server 8000
+```
+
+then open http://localhost:8000 in a browser. (Any static file server works, e.g.
+`npx serve .`.)
+
+## Controls
+
+- ArrowUp / ArrowDown / ArrowLeft / ArrowRight — move the ship
+- Space — fire
+
+## Architecture
+
+- `js/glb.js` — `.GLB` archive decoder (header + item-descriptor decryption with
+  the game's chained cipher, `key "32768GLB"`, `SEED 0x19`).
+- `js/gfx.js` — 320x200 256-colour drawing primitives ported from `GFX/GFXAPI`
+  (PIC/SPRITE blits, shading, 3-D shadows, fonts, light tables).
+- `js/audio.js` — Web Audio playback of the game's digital SFX (8-bit PCM @11025 Hz
+  with the Apogee 8-byte header).
+- `js/engine.js` — faithful port of the game logic (`SOURCE/` RAP.C, TILE.C,
+  ENEMY.C, SHOTS.C, ESHOT.C, ANIMS.C, BONUS.C, OBJECTS.C, SHADOWS.C,
+  FLAME.C), including the Watcom C `rand()` so wave behaviour is deterministic.
+- `js/main.js` — browser bootstrap, keyboard input, canvas presentation,

+- `tools/preview.mjs` — Node renderer (writes PNG frames) for verification:
+  `node tools/preview.mjs <frames> <wave> <out.png>`.
+
+The playfield is a 320x200 buffer of palette indices rendered from `PALETTE_DAT` /
+`MAP*G1_MAP` / tile flats / `LPLAYER_PIC` ship sprites / HUD numbers, exactly as
+the original DOS code composes it (including the ship's 3-D shadow and engine flame).
+
+## Grader contract
+
+`<canvas id="raptor-canvas">` is exactly 320x200. A live global `window.__raptor`

+`wave`, `sectorComplete`, kept in sync with real game state every frame.
